findings: 2026-11-06: drafted for Mathematics 12 Unit 3 (owner request): English and a teacher-style Roman Urdu lesson; the book's content in order with our clearly labelled teaching notes; worked examples step by step with reasons; results verified with sympy.

Book correction: The book prints the right-hand integral of Property-VIII with lower limit c: \int_{c}^{b} g(x)\,dx. Both integrals run over the same interval [a, b]. Correct: \int_{a}^{b} f(x)\,dx \le \int_{a}^{b} g(x)\,dx

Book correction: Example 50 has three printing slips: 1. The sub-intervals are printed as [-6, 2], [-2, 1], [1, 4]. The first one is [-6, -2] (part (a) of the book's own solution uses [-6, -2]). 2. Part (c) prints only |x - 1| and leaves out = x - 1. 3. The final sum is printed as 28 + 9 + 18 = 57. The sum is 55, so \int_{-6}^{4} f(x)\,dx = 55.
Book correction: Example 52 is printed as the bare integral \int_{0}^{2\pi} \cos^{5} x\,dx without an instruction. It means: Evaluate \int_{0}^{2\pi} \cos^{5} x\,dx.

Book correction: The statement of Example 56 prints only Evaluate \int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx; the data needed appear only inside the solution. The full question is: Given \int_{0}^{2} f(x)\,dx = 4 and f(2 - x) = f(x) = f(-x), evaluate \int_{1}^{3} f(x)\,dx.
